title: A certification reaches CC's bus address
owner: cairn (cairn/tools/base is the base tool's address; CC builds)
intention: Each certification a gate issues (a ticket's crossing, journaled by emit) reaches CC's bus address as one 'personal' message, so CC, today's builder, prover and every other summons handler, hears the event without standing at the gate.
why: Akien 2026-10-27, verbatim on open-a89d15043c7c: 'that certification being completed is an event. that event triggers probes for any device in the system that can handle that event... over the bus. no orchestrator'; on open-c345acf7f373: 'right now you are the builder and the prover and the so on... we can build out the pieces that would send you email for each of these event changes'; on open-a44f6aadde21: 'a message to your bus address', because mail is an open prompt-injection hole.
traces_to: Akien's answers on open-a89d15043c7c, open-c345acf7f373, open-a44f6aadde21; the bus intention (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/intention+why.json: the only device-to-device path); Law 1; ticket 1e2640bad4dd (PROVED: the receiving half, bus -> CC mailbox -> poke); ticket 48519f4789b1 decision 14 (the removed post this answers).
how: A gate's probes are JSON files in instance-space, one per probe, at ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/machines/gate/<gate>/probes/ (D8). A new tool module cairn/tools/base/gate_probes.py loads, seeds, clears and fires them (D10, D12). emit in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py, right after projector.append_entry journals a ticket-carrying crossing at a class-space address, calls gate_probes.fire for the gate the crossing entered; each probe whose event is 'certified' becomes one 'personal' envelope to its 'to' through the one bus process (RemoteBus; never ensure_bus/connect_bus), carrying the crossing's fields, the rendered message and the testing mark when set (D3, D4, D9). Every failure is caught and reported on stderr; the crossing already stands (D5). Seeded with one cc probe per gate. CC's shim (built, 1e2640bad4dd) delivers and pokes. Decisions D2-D5 and D7-D12; D1 and D6 were superseded into D7 and removed.
falsifier: DONE when (1) a live crossing of a real ticket puts exactly one 'personal' envelope to 'cc' with verb 'certified' on the bus naming that ticket, component and summons, and ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/mail_ledger.jsonl shows it delivered (plus 'poked' if CC was idle); (2) with the bus unreachable, emit still journals, returns the new workflow string and raises nothing; (3) under CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID the body carries testing_mark.mark(<id>). (2)-(3) are proofs in cairn/tools/base/proofs/; (1) is measured live at PROVEME. WRONG INTENT if the mail-ledger rate shows notices CC never acts on, or if a second handler makes the address 'cc' a consumer registry, in which case the event moves to subscription.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [FIXME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> PROVED
watchme: none, because the falsifier's noise question is read directly from CC's mail ledger at /home/akien/.cairn/devices/cc/0/mail_ledger.jsonl, which the cc device's mail probe already counts (ticket 1e2640bad4dd).

decisions.text: D2: PLACE. The post runs in emit after projector.append_entry and before _stamp_sail. The D14 comment at that spot is rewritten to cite this ticket and say how both of D14's whys are answered: the one bus process replaces the unflushed private ring, and the post comes after the journal, off the verdict path. Import lazily inside the function; never call ensure_bus or connect_bus (they spawn a bus).

D3: BODY. {ticket, component (history_path's parent relative to the cairn root), from, to, direction ('forward'|'back'), fingerprint (record['fingerprint'])}. Never ticket content: CC reads the ticket through its own door. why = 'certified: <ticket> <from> -> <to>'. Every ticket-carrying crossing emit journals is sent, forward and back; noise is measured from the mail ledger, never filtered by a rule written before measurement.

D4: TESTING. When os.environ has CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID, the body carries 'testing': cairn.tools.base.testing_mark.mark(that id), so CC's shim returns it unacted on (Akien: 'testing things are marked as such and we just demand that the system can tolerate and ignore them').

D5: NEVER GATES. Every exception from import, connect or post is caught; one line goes to stderr naming the ticket and the error, and emit returns as before (Law 7: the journal is the record of truth). Proofs live in cairn/tools/base/proofs/ with a stand-in RemoteBus, binding the subject at call time: one tooth for the envelope shape, one for the unreachable bus, one for the testing mark.

D7: A GATE'S PROBES, superseding D6's coined 'handler list'. Akien 2026-10-27: 'each device can add probes to a gate... a list of handlers and data to give them as opposed to probes that are compiled in to pieces of python' and ''handler list' you mean the probes? a probe can be a lot of things. a probe can be a json packet: { event: eventname, message: {event} on {ticket} }, or a surgically implanted piece of code that reports back some metric.' So the gate holds a list of probes, and certification fires each one. This ticket builds the data kind only: a JSON probe {to: <bus address>, event: <eventname>, message: '<template over {event} and {ticket}>'}, fired as one 'personal' envelope to its 'to', whose body is D3's fields plus the rendered message. The code kind (cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe, with trigger/carry callables) is untouched and out of scope here. Today the list holds one probe: {to: 'cc', event: 'certified', message: '{event} on {ticket}'}. Where a gate's probes live is open-413b07bf8322.

D8: WHERE A GATE'S PROBES LIVE (Akien 2026-10-27, open-413b07bf8322 and open-a0e22798522e): at the gate, in instance-space, one JSON file per probe: '~/.cairn/devices/codemother/machines/gate/build/probes/*.json <- the json files point to the handlers that get notified that this ticket is ready for them.' With the instance segment CLAUDE.md requires (a singleton is 0), the path is ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/machines/gate/<gate>/probes/*.json. <gate> is the summons the crossing enters with ME dropped and lowercased (BUILDME -> build, PROVEME -> prove, FIXME -> fix, WATCHME -> watch, TICKETME -> ticket), and PROVED -> proved; CC's call, overridable. At certification, emit reads that folder and fires each probe (D7's JSON shape). A missing or empty folder fires nothing. A malformed probe file is reported on stderr and skipped, never gating. 'Clear all the probes across all devices for <device>' is a verb that deletes every probes/*.json under ~/.cairn/devices/*/*/machines/gate/*/ whose 'to' is <device>. Seeded today with one probe per gate: {to: 'cc', event: 'certified', message: '{event} on {ticket}'}.

D9: FIRING. The event of every crossing is 'certified'. For each probe file in the entered gate's folder, in filename order, whose 'event' equals 'certified', post one envelope through RemoteBus: sender 'cairn', to=probe['to'], channel 'personal', verb=probe['event'], why=the rendered message, body = D3's six fields + {'probe': <file stem>, 'message': <rendered>} + D4's 'testing' when set. Rendering is str.format(event=probe['event'], ticket=<ticket id>) and nothing else. A probe whose event is not 'certified' fires nothing today. A malformed probe is reported on stderr and skipped: not a JSON object, a missing or non-string to/event/message, or a template naming any other key. The rendered message replaces D3's why.

D10: SEED AND CLEAR. New module cairn/tools/base/gate_probes.py owns the folder, with every path built from cairn.tools.base.address.instance_path('codemother', 0, roots)/'machines'/'gate'/<gate>/'probes' (the roots argument lets proofs point at a temp dir). GATES = ('build','prove','fix','watch','ticket','proved'). gate_for(summons) maps BUILDME->build, PROVEME->prove, FIXME->fix, WATCHME->watch, TICKETME->ticket, PROVED->proved, and anything else to None, which fires nothing. load(gate, roots=None) returns (probes, errors). seed(device, roots=None) writes <device>.json = {to: device, event: 'certified', message: '{event} on {ticket}'} into each of the six gates and leaves an existing file untouched. clear(device, roots=None) deletes every devices/*/*/machines/gate/*/probes/*.json under the instance root whose 'to' is device and returns the deleted paths. CLI: python3 -m cairn.tools.base.gate_probes seed|clear|list <device>. The live step runs 'seed cc' once. emit's firing function (D2) calls load().

D11: PROOFS (extends D5's teeth). Proofs live in cairn/tools/base/proofs/ over a temp roots table and a stand-in RemoteBus, binding the subject at call time. Teeth: envelope shape (one probe, one personal envelope with D9's fields); unreachable bus (emit returns and journals, nothing raises); testing mark under CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID; missing or empty folder posts nothing; malformed probe skipped with a stderr line while a good sibling still fires; seed writes six files and is idempotent; clear removes only the named device's files.

D12: API AND SCOPE. gate_probes.load(gate, roots=None) returns (probes, errors): probes is a list of (file_stem, dict) in filename order, and errors is a list of strings. gate_probes.fire(*, ticket, component, from_, to, direction, fingerprint, roots=None, bus=None) does D9's posting; bus=None means cairn.tools.bus_client.remote.RemoteBus() (no args = the live bus home), posted as bus.post(sender='cairn', to=..., channel='personal', why=..., verb=..., body=...). A missing socket raises FileNotFoundError or ConnectionRefusedError, which D5 catches. In emit, history_path is emit's own keyword argument. When it is None, or does not resolve under the cairn repo root (Path(transitions.__file__).resolve().parents[3]), or the crossing carries no ticket in journal_extra, nothing fires: a proof's temp-dir crossing never reaches the live bus. Otherwise emit computes component = history_path's parent relative to that root and calls gate_probes.fire inside D5's catch-all. Proof files follow cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_crossing_fingerprint.py: plain test_* functions plus a __main__ runner, exit 0 = green. The proof stand-in bus is an object whose post(**kw) appends kw to a list (or raises ConnectionRefusedError for the unreachable tooth), passed as bus=.

D2A: THE D14 COMMENT, located. It stands in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py emit, directly under 'projector.append_entry(history_path, state_path, record)' (line 2355 at HEAD e52c486c), and begins '# No bus post to harbor_master here (removed, ticket 48519f4789b1 decision 14).' Its two whys: the post went through a private BusDevice whose ring nothing flushed (563 notices to 2026-09-02, none since), and posting through the one bus process would put a socket on the inspector's verdict path, since the inspector imports this module. Replace those six lines with a comment citing 32f500e517d7 that answers both: the one bus process (RemoteBus) replaces the private ring, and the post runs after the journal, inside a catch-all, only for class-space crossings (D12), so it never decides a verdict. The firing call goes right after that comment, still inside the 'if history_path' block.

D3A: FIELD MAP. In emit's gated record (transitions.py ~line 2288): from = record['from'] (wf.here, the summons left), to = record['to'] (target, the summons entered, which also picks the gate via gate_for), direction = record['direction'] ('forward'|'back'), fingerprint = record['fingerprint'], ticket = journal_extra['ticket']. A disposition (the early-return branch with direction 'disposition', ~line 2125) passes no gate, so it is not a certification and fires nothing: no call is added there.

D10A: WHEN SEED RUNS. Once, by hand, by the builder at the live-fire step after PROVEME: 'python3 -m cairn.tools.base.gate_probes seed cc'. Never at startup, install or on any beat: probes are data a device adds when it wants to hear a gate, and an empty folder firing nothing is the agreed default (Akien 2026-10-27, 'agreed on empty folder fires nothing'). The PROVED crossing is then the first live fire that reaches CC.

D12A: HOLDINGS MEASURED at HEAD e52c486c (each exists, nothing to build): cairn/tools/base/address.py:instance_path(device: str, instance: int = 0, roots: dict[str, Path] | None = None) -> Path, giving <instance root>/devices/<device>/<instance>, where roots={'repo','commons','instance'} paths; cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py:RemoteBus(home=None) with no args = the live bus home, and RemoteBus.post(**kw) forwards to the bus process's BusDevice.post(*, sender, to, channel, why, verb='', body=None, reply_to=None) (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py:426); cairn/tools/base/testing_mark.py:mark(test: str, kind='return') -> dict, and its FIELD = 'testing' is the body key.

Teeth 2 and 9 pass emit node_class_root resolved as the sibling CairnCommons/node_classes if present, else ~/dev/src/CairnCommons/node_classes, so they run in hollow's commons-less worktree; no build code changes.

Teeth 2 and 9 are tooth_an_unreachable_bus_never_gates_the_crossing and tooth_emit_fires_after_the_journal; transitions.emit already takes node_class_root (default _NODE_CLASSES). The repair is done and committed (86905328): a module-level _NODE_CLASSES = <repo>.parent/CairnCommons/node_classes if that dir exists else ~/dev/src/CairnCommons/node_classes, passed as node_class_root= in both emit calls; green 9/9 twice live and in a commons-less worktree. Next is the BUILDME re-cross naming this proof, then PROVEME, seal and hollow.
